chunks: There is nothing (payable as Zakat) in less than twenty mithqal of gold. So when twenty mithqal are complete, then half a mithqal (is payable) up to twenty-four. So when twenty-four are complete, then three-fifths of a dinar (is payable) up to twenty-eight. Thus it continues on this accounting: every time it increases by four.

key_terms.أخماس دينار: Fifths of a dinar — the zakat rate on amounts above twenty-four mithqal
key_terms.مثقال: Mithqal — a unit of weight equal to approximately 4.25 grams; twenty mithqal equals roughly 85 grams of gold
key_terms.نصاب: Nisab — the minimum threshold of wealth subject to zakat
key_terms.نصف مثقال: Half a mithqal — the zakat rate on twenty mithqal of gold, equivalent to 2.5% of the nisab
key_terms.هذا الحساب: This accounting — the incremental formula for calculating zakat on gold exceeding the basic rates

ai.seo_question: What is the nisab and zakat rate for gold according to Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them) establishes the nisab (minimum threshold) and incremental zakat rates for gold. The nisab is twenty mithqal (approximately 85 grams), below which no zakat is due. For every four mithqal above twenty, a proportionate amount is added — the hadith provides a formulaic rule rather than listing all possible amounts. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for calculating zakat on gold.
